title: Platform systems & services — dashboards, alerts, runbooks, retrospective, and roadmap (Q2 2026 addendum)
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Summary:
This page centralizes guidance for Platform Systems & Services: system ownership, canonical dashboards, alert thresholds, operational runbooks, recent retrospectives, and the Q2 2026 roadmap addendum. It is intended as the single source of truth for on-call engineers, platform owners, and cross-functional stakeholders.

Goals:
- Reduce time-to-detect and time-to-recover for platform degradations (target MTTR < 30 minutes for Sev2; < 4 hours for Sev3).
- Maintain platform SLOs: 99.9% availability for API gateway and 99.95% for core serving runtime (monthly).
- Standardize dashboards and alerts to reduce cognitive overhead during incidents.

Owners and contacts:
- Platform Systems & Services (primary): platform-team@redwood.example.com
- On-call rotation: platform-oncall
- Pager duty escalation: see team wiki -> "oncall-and-escalation"
- Document owner: Aisha Patel (platform engineering)

1) Systems & services inventory (high-level)
- api-gateway (service): handles external REST/SDK traffic, rate limiting, auth enforcement. Owner: api-platform.
- serving-runtime (service): GPU-optimized inference runtime. Owner: eng-serving-runtime.
- request-router (service): smart routing, fallbacks, multi-region routing. Owner: platform-routing-team.
- cache-layer (service): prefix/KV caching for inference sessions. Owner: platform-caching.
- telemetry-pipeline (service): metrics/logs/traces ingestion and retention. Owner: observability-team.

2) Canonical dashboards (what to open first)
Open these dashboards when an alert fires or during daily checks:
- Platform Overview (summary): traffic, error rate, p50/p95/p99 latency, token throughput, capacity headroom.
- API Gateway Health: 5xx rate, auth failures, rate-limit rejections, pod restarts.
- Serving Runtime: GPU utilization per cluster, KV cache hit rate, KV miss latency, tail request latency, queue depth.
- Request Router: routing failures, fallback rate, cross-region failover events.
- Telemetry Pipeline: ingestion lag, write error rate, storage utilization.

Dashboard best practices:
- Always include the time picker set to 6 hours for incident debug, 30 days for trend analysis.
- Use p95/p99 for latency SLO indicators; use p50 for capacity smoothing.
- Annotate dashboards with recent deploys and known incident windows (upper-right corner).

3) Alerts and thresholds (defaults)
Note: Teams may tune thresholds per-service but must preserve global severity mapping and paging behavior.
Severity mapping:
- Sev1 (pager to oncall + channel): total system outage (availability < 90%), sustained high error rate (> 10% 5xx for 5+ mins), or data-loss events.
- Sev2 (pager to oncall): significant degradation (availability 90-98%, p99 latency > 5s sustained 5 mins), token throughput < 50% capacity for 10+ mins.
- Sev3 (channel only): minor degradations, non-urgent spikes, or noisy telemetry issues.

Default alert rules (examples):
| Service | Metric | Condition | Severity | Owner |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| api-gateway | 5xx-rate | > 5% over 5m | Sev2 | api-platform |
| serving-runtime | gpu-utilization | > 92% on > 50% nodes for 10m | Sev2 | eng-serving-runtime |
| serving-runtime | queue-depth | > 2000 on ingress for 5m | Sev1 | platform-systems |
| cache-layer | kv-hit-rate | < 70% for 10m | Sev2 | platform-caching |
| telemetry-pipeline | ingestion-lag | > 5m for > 10% shards | Sev2 | observability-team |

Alert lifecycle and rules:
1. Alerts must include a short description, steps-to-take, runbook link, and runbook run_id when triggered.
2. First responder must acknowledge within 5 minutes for Sev1/Sev2.
3. If not resolved within 30 minutes for Sev1, escalate to engineering manager and SRE lead; create incident in incident tracker.

4) Operational runbooks (templates and examples)
Structure for every runbook (required fields):
- Runbook title
- Owner and author
- Preconditions/when to use
- Dashboard(s) to open
- Step-by-step mitigation (numbered)
- Post-incident tasks and RCA checklist
- Related pages and playbooks

Example runbook: "Serving runtime high tail latency"
Preconditions: sustained p99 > 4s for 5+ minutes or queue-depth growing > 10% over baseline.
Dashboards: Serving Runtime, GPU utilization, Cache Layer
Steps:
1) Triage: confirm p99 and queue depth on Serving Runtime dashboard. Note deploy annotations.
2) If GPU utilization > 95%: scale horizontal replicas by +20% (kubectl scale deployment serving-runtime --replicas=<n>).
3) If queue-depth not decreasing after scale: open throttling window on API Gateway / increase batching timeout to reduce head-of-line blocking.
4) If KV cache miss rate increased: check cache servers for OOMs/connection failures; restart affected cache pods (kubectl rollout restart sts cache-cluster).
5) If root cause unclear after steps 1-4: failover traffic to warm backup region (see Request Router runbook) and create incident.
Post-incident:
- Capture timeline and create follow-up ticket tagged "postmortem/serving-latency-<YYYYMMDD>"
- Run automated load-tests against fixed branch before merge of any mitigation code.

5) Runbook change process
- All runbook edits must be reviewed by at least one oncall reviewer and an SRE reviewer.
- For any runbook that changes paging behavior or escalation steps, run a tabletop exercise during next game-day.
- Use the prefix runbook/v1, runbook/v1.1 in the runbook header for version tracking.

6) Retrospective summary (last 90 days)
Top incidents and actions:
- Incident: Increased p99 latency on serving-runtime (2025-11-12)
  - Root cause: regression in batching scheduler + an untested quantization profile under high concurrency.
  - Action: Add integration test for batching+quantization; adjust default quantization profile for high-concurrency customers.
- Incident: Telemetry pipeline ingestion lag (2025-12-07)
  - Root cause: retention compaction causing GC spikes on ingestion nodes.
  - Action: Stagger compaction jobs; increase ingestion buffer size by 25%.
- Action items completed:
  - New integration test added to CI for batching (owned by eng-serving-runtime).
  - Dashboard annotations now show deploy IDs and owner contact by default.

Retro themes and follow-ups:
- Improve load-testing coverage for mixed workloads (short+long sequences). Owner: applied-ml-and-evals.
- Better pre-deploy smoke checks for telemetry compaction. Owner: observability-team.
- Quarterly tabletop for runbook changes that affect paging. Owner: platform-team.

7) Q2 2026 roadmap (addendum)
Planned work (Q2):
- Standardize dashboard templates (owner: observability-team) — deliverable: "platform-dashboard-template-v1" (end of Apr 2026).
- Alert suppression framework: allow scheduled maintenance windows and deploy-time suppressions (owner: platform-infra) — Beta (May 2026).
- Runbook authoring UX: add structured fields and automated link-to-incident in Confluence template (owner: platform-team) — rollout (Jun 2026).
- Capacity automation: predictive scaling for serving-runtime based on moving-window token forecasts (owner: eng-sre) — prototype (Jun 2026).

Roadmap priorities and acceptance criteria:
- Each deliverable must include: owner, success metric (e.g., reduce false positive alerts by 30%), target date, and monitoring plan.
- Any change that shifts paging must be communicated to on-call rotations at least 2 weeks prior and accompanied by a tabletop.

8) Playbooks and how-tos (quick links)
- How to add an alert rule (step-by-step)
  1) Open the Alerting UI -> New Rule.
  2) Select metric and set threshold; attach runbook link and short remediation steps.
  3) Set severity tag and ownership group.
  4) Add alert annotations: runbook id, owner, revert playbook id.
- How to create a dashboard from template
  1) Open Dashboard Templates -> Platform Overview Template.
  2) Customize time ranges and variable (cluster, region).
  3) Save as "<team>-platform-overview-<YYYYMM>" and notify observability-team for indexing.

9) Team wiki & knowledge hygiene
- Keep runbooks under the /confluence/eng-platform/runbooks namespace and include a last-reviewed date on the header.
- Quarterly review: each runbook must be reviewed by owner and one cross-team reviewer.
- Tag retired services with label "retired" and archive runbooks to the archive space with a short summary.

10) Appendix — emergency commands and links
- Scale serving runtime (k8s): kubectl -n platform scale deployment serving-runtime --replicas=<N>
- Restart cache statefulset: kubectl -n platform rollout restart statefulset cache-cluster
- Failover router execution (internal CLI): rtr failover --region us-west-2 --drain-grace 60s
- Incident template: /confluence/eng-platform/templates/incident-template

If you are the on-call and this document is unclear at any step, escalate to the SRE lead and follow the incident escalation playbook.
